claim_under_test: For pure deterministic typed local transitions, a sparse epoch-bound semantic commutator can match full two-order replay for order sensitivity while exposing more safe independence than conservative read/write conflicts at lower cost than full-state replay.
primary_baselines: FULL_REPLAY: apply both operations in both orders to complete 512-dimensional state
RW_CONFLICT: conservative read/write overlap declares conflict
NO_CANDIDATE: equivalent to current conservative/fixed coordination for this proxy
controls: SHUFFLED: shuffle commutator labels while preserving prevalence
STALE_EPOCH: perturb 25% of base state while reusing old commutator decision
RESOURCE_MATCHED_FULL_PLUS_RW: spend only local-commutator wall-clock on full replays, use conservative RW for remainder
success_criteria: zero false-commute labels on eligible synthetic operations
exact match to full replay on generated pure deterministic transition class
safe-independence fraction greater than RW conflict baseline
local commutator materially cheaper than full replay
stale-state control must demonstrate why epoch binding is required rather than silently remaining trusted
automatic_failure_conditions: any effect-authority inference from proxy result
any promotion to target-supported without H1/H2/target-VPS evidence
any reuse of commutator receipt across mismatched state instance/epoch
